messages:
sara: Customer NimbleHealth reports that responses became noticeably more terse after a model push to v9.1.3 yesterday. They say otherwise-similar prompts now return much shorter replies. Can @olivia / @raj take a look?

raj: Can you paste the exact user prompt and both outputs (before/after)? Also any curl repro they used.

sara: Paste from customer (redacted):
```
User: Explain diabetes management to a patient in plain terms with examples.
```
They included two outputs:
• before (v9.0.8): "Managing diabetes means watching blood sugar. Start by checking levels daily, follow a balanced meal plan, take medicines as prescribed, and watch for signs like increased thirst. Example: a healthy breakfast could be..." (~180 words, friendly tone)
• after (v9.1.3): "Manage blood sugar: check regularly, follow diet and meds. Example: choose whole grains, avoid sugary drinks." (~45 words, more direct)

sara: Their repro curl is:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-v9.1.3","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Explain diabetes management to a patient in plain terms with examples."}],"temperature":0.2,"max_tokens":250}'
```

olivia: Noted. Quick check: deploy-bot shows v9.1.3 went to prod on us-west1 at 1728986400. I'll pull the model config diffs and recent tuning changes.

deploy-bot: Deploy finished: model redwood-chat-v9.1.3 -> production (us-west1) @1728986400

raj: Two hypothesis: 1) a new brevity tuning/decoding bias was enabled to reduce latency, 2) default system prompt got tightened. Can we confirm which changed between v9.0.8 and v9.1.3?

olivia: Checking commit log... I see a small change flagged "brevity_bias: 0.15" added in the generation config to shave avg token count for common instruction prompts. That would produce shorter replies.

raj: Can you reproduce locally toggling brevity_bias? I'll run the same curl but override any client-side param we can.

olivia: Try this repro with explicit override:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-v9.1.3","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Explain diabetes management to a patient in plain terms with examples."}],"temperature":0.2,"max_tokens":250,"generation_overrides":{"brevity_bias":0.0}}'
```

raj: Quick test results (local):
• v9.1.3 default brevity_bias=0.15 -> output length ~50 words, tone = curt
• v9.1.3 with brevity_bias=0.0 -> output length ~170 words, tone ~= v9.0.8
So brevity_bias matches the regression.

sara: Customer asks for mitigation now — they prefer previous verbosity. Options? rollback or client-side override instructions.

olivia: Short-term: tell customer to set generation_overrides.brevity_bias=0.0 (we can give curl snippet). Medium-term: we'll open an internal PR to revert brevity default and run full eval suite for regressions. Long-term: add eval guard for instruction-length delta.

sara: I'll send the customer the curl with generation_overrides and offer a canary rollback if they want service-level fix. They're asking for a rollback if the override is insufficient.

kenneth: FYI SRE: rollback window tonight at 02:00 PT is available if eng-ml approves; note SLA impact for canary traffic.

olivia: Opening INC ticket: INC-2026-1789. I'll attach diffs, eval plots, and the reproduction script. Planning PR to revert brevity_bias default and run gated canary. Will update here when CI passes.

sara: Customer updated: they tested the override and confirm responses look like before. They're happy with workaround but want permanent fix. I flagged INC to their account team. :thumbsup:

raj: Putting a short checklist in the ticket: reproduce, confirm metric impact (latency/cost delta), run evals on 10K prompts, revert if quality drop > threshold.

olivia: Agreed. I'll coordinate with infra for a fast rollback if the evals show larger downstream impacts.

sara: Thanks all — keeping thread open for PR + rollback decision.
